name.text: Reading a graph: water in a tank over time

questiontext.text:
The amount of water in a tank was recorded at different times. The graph shows the recorded amounts (the dots) and the line or curve drawn through them.

(a) Use the graph to find the amount of water in the tank after \( {@t1@} \) minutes.

Amount of water = [[input:ans1]] litres [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Use the graph to find the time taken for the tank to contain \( {@V2@} \) litres of water.

Time taken = [[input:ans2]] minutes [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

questionvariables.text:
/* ---------- DESIGN BACKWARDS: every value the student must read sits exactly on a grid-line intersection ---------- Volume after t minutes: V(t) = c0 + c1 t + c2 t^2 + c3 t^3 litres, always strictly increasing on [0, T]. shp 1: straight line (constant fill rate) shp 2: curve getting steeper (fills faster and faster) shp 3: curve flattening (fills more and more slowly) shp 4: S-shaped (slow, then fast, then slow) Pool entry [shp, c0, c1, c2, c3, T, u, dt, t1, t2]: c0 litres in the tank at t = 0 (a multiple of u, so the start is on a grid line) T the graph runs from t = 0 to t = T minutes (8, 10 or 12) u vertical grid spacing in litres (5, 10, 20, 25 or 50); horizontal grid spacing is 1 minute dt the amount is RECORDED every dt minutes (a dot on the graph) t1 part (a): "how many litres after t1 minutes?" -> V1 = V(t1) is a whole multiple of u t2 part (b): "how long to reach V2 litres?" -> V2 = V(t2) is a whole multiple of u, t2 a whole number Neither t1 nor t2 is a recorded time, so the student must read the line or curve itself (any point along the time axis). The diagnosed wrong answers (time instead of volume, one grid line out, volume instead of time ...) are always different numbers. */ pool : [ [3,20,42,-2,0,10,20,2,5,1], [2,0,2,1,0,12,20,3,10,8], [3,0,16,-1/2,0,12,10,3,10,2], [1,0,8,0,0,12,20,3,5,10], [4,50,0,4,-1/5,12,25,3,10,5], [1,50,10,0,0,12,50,3,5,10], [2,0,1,1/2,0,12,20,3,10,8], [2,0,0,2,0,12,50,3,10,5], [2,50,0,2,0,12,50,3,10,5], [3,50,50,-2,0,12,50,3,10,5], [3,0,14,-1/2,0,12,10,3,8,10], [3,20,24,-1,0,12,20,3,4,10], [1,10,5,0,0,8,5,2,1,5], [2,10,1,1,0,10,10,2,9,5], [3,0,42,-2,0,10,20,2,5,1], [2,20,1,1/2,0,12,10,3,10,8], [4,0,0,4,-1/5,12,25,3,10,5], [3,40,28,-1,0,12,20,3,8,10], [1,40,4,0,0,12,10,3,5,10], [2,40,2,1,0,12,20,3,8,10], [3,10,12,-1/2,0,12,10,3,10,4], [2,20,1,1/2,0,12,20,3,10,8], [1,40,12,0,0,12,20,3,5,10], [2,0,1,1/2,0,12,10,3,8,10], [1,0,15,0,0,12,25,3,10,5], [2,0,0,1,0,12,25,3,10,5], [2,0,4,1/2,0,12,10,3,2,10], [2,40,1,1/2,0,12,20,3,8,10], [3,20,28,-1,0,12,20,3,8,10], [1,0,25,0,0,8,25,2,3,7], [3,0,28,-1,0,12,20,3,10,8], [2,0,1,1,0,10,10,2,5,9], [1,10,5,0,0,12,10,3,10,8], [1,40,20,0,0,10,20,2,9,7], [1,40,10,0,0,12,20,3,2,10], [3,20,34,-2,0,8,20,2,5,7], [3,20,12,-1/2,0,12,10,3,4,10], [3,30,12,-1/2,0,12,10,3,10,4], [3,40,34,-2,0,8,20,2,5,7], [2,0,0,2,0,12,25,3,5,10], [2,50,0,1,0,12,25,3,10,5], [2,20,2,2,0,10,20,2,5,9], [2,0,2,2,0,10,20,2,9,5], [2,10,1,1/2,0,12,10,3,8,10], [2,20,2,1,0,12,20,3,8,10], [3,40,12,-1/2,0,12,10,3,10,4], [1,0,5,0,0,12,5,2,3,11], [1,50,4,0,0,12,10,3,5,10], [1,0,8,0,0,12,10,3,10,5], [3,0,24,-1,0,12,20,3,4,10], [1,10,4,0,0,12,10,3,5,10], [1,20,20,0,0,8,20,2,7,5], [3,0,50,-2,0,12,50,3,5,10], [3,0,12,-1/2,0,12,10,3,10,4], [3,0,34,-2,0,8,20,2,5,7], [1,50,15,0,0,12,25,3,10,5], [1,20,5,0,0,12,10,3,4,8], [2,30,1,1/2,0,12,10,3,10,8], [1,50,25,0,0,10,25,2,9,7], [1,10,10,0,0,10,10,2,3,5], [3,10,14,-1/2,0,12,10,3,8,10], [1,10,4,0,0,12,5,3,5,10] ]; /* ANSWER (a): litres after t1 minutes */ V2 : Vf(t2); /* the target volume in part (b); ANSWER (b) is t2 minutes */ Vend : Vf(TT); Vtop : uu*ceiling(Vend/uu) + uu; /* top of the vertical axis (a multiple of u) */ shpTxt : if is(shp=1) then "The graph is a straight line, so the tank fills at a constant rate." else if is(shp=2) then "The graph curves upward and gets steeper, so the tank fills faster and faster." else if is(shp=3) then "The graph curves but flattens, so the tank fills more and more slowly." else "The graph is S-shaped: the tank fills slowly at first, then faster, then slowly again."; rate : if is(shp=1) then (Vend - V0)/TT else 0; chkA : if is(shp=1) then sconcat("

Check. The graph is a straight line, so the tank fills at a constant rate: from ", string(V0), " to ", string(Vend), " litres in ", string(TT), " minutes is ", string(rate), " litres every minute. After ", string(t1), " minutes the tank holds ", string(V0), " + ", string(rate), " x ", string(t1), " = ", string(V1), " litres.

") else sconcat("

Why we read the curve itself. ", shpTxt, " The amount does not rise by the same number of litres every minute, so there is no single rate to multiply by. The value has to be read from the curve, where the vertical grid line for ", string(t1), " minutes meets it.

"); chkB : if is(shp=1) then sconcat("

") else sconcat("

"); qnote : sconcat("shape ", string(shp), " c=", string(c0), ",", string(c1), ",", string(c2), ",", string(c3), " T=", string(TT), " u=", string(uu), " dt=", string(dtt), " t1=", string(t1), " V2=", string(V2));

node.description: gave the time instead of the volume

truefeedback.text: That number is the time, which is read on the horizontal axis. The question asks for the amount of water, which is read on the vertical axis: go up from the time to the graph, then across to the vertical axis.

node.description: one grid line out; otherwise generic

truefeedback.text: You are exactly one grid line out. Look at the vertical axis: each grid line stands for a fixed number of litres, so check which grid line the graph meets.

falsefeedback.text: That is not the amount of water at that time. Find the time on the horizontal axis, go straight up to the graph, then straight across to the vertical axis and read the value.

truefeedback.text: That is the amount of water given in the question. The question asks for the time, which is read on the horizontal axis: go across from the amount to the graph, then straight down to the time axis.
You are exactly one grid line out. Each vertical grid line on the time axis is 1 minute: check which grid line the point on the graph is on.

falsefeedback.text: That is not the time at which the tank holds that amount. Find the amount on the vertical axis, go across to the graph, then straight down to the horizontal (time) axis.
